conclusion: No evidence of target-result leakage in the saved Bahrain modeling pipeline under these tests.

checks.check: Training cutoff and target field allowlist
checks.detail: 330 rows from rounds 1–15; 22 Bahrain qualifying rows, no target outcome fields.
Every recorded data/code SHA-256 matches the original forecast artifact.
All 352 driver rows agree with independently calculated strictly-prior-race features.
Changing current/future outcomes cannot change the features for any of rounds 1–15.
Six prohibited field types and Bahrain rows injected into training are rejected by production validation.
Training-row shuffling and consistent driver/team anonymization preserve fitted coefficients and target features.
Entire prediction JSON reproduced exactly, including selection, probabilities and validation; original project/workbooks and network access blocked.
Real labels: 1.889/3 mean hits; shuffled labels: 0.430/3. See caveats; this is supporting evidence, not proof.

negative_control.protocol: 30 within-race label permutations; fixed original four-feature model, chronological held-outs 7–15; form recomputed. Descriptive control, not a calibrated significance test.

limitations: Cannot certify upstream workbook labels or the exact historical publication state of qualifying pages.
Hashes demonstrate consistency with saved artifacts, not independently timestamped provenance.
Italian forecast had incidental assistant search exposure; code audit cannot make the full conversation blind.
Repeated model development on known history and a small sample limit claims about generalization.
No Bahrain actual outcome is used in these tests or model fitting.
